units.text: INT. SUPERMAN - CONTINUOUS
I was brute enough to do so last night.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Brute enough! What do you mean?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: dithyrambically.
Jack: we men are all coarse. We never understand how exquisite a woman's sensibilities are. How could I have done such a thing!
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Done what, you maudlin idiot?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Yes, I am an idiot. Jack: if you had heard her voice! if you had seen her tears! I have lain awake all night thinking of them. If she had reproached me, I could have borne it better.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Tears! that's dangerous. What did she say?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: She asked me how she could think of anything now but her dear father. She stifled a sob--
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: he breaks down.
patting him on the back.
Bear it like a man, Tavy, even if you feel it like an ass. It's the old game: she's not tired of playing with you yet.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: impatiently.
Oh, don't be a fool, Jack. Do you suppose this eternal shallow cynicism of yours has any real bearing on a nature like hers?
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Hm! Did she say anything else?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Yes; and that is why I expose myself and her to your ridicule by telling you what passed.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: remorsefully.
No, dear Tavy, not ridicule, on my honor! However, no matter. Go on.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Her sense of duty is so devout, so perfect, so--
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Yes: I know. Go on.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: You see, under this new arrangement, you and Ramsden are her guardians; and she considers that all her duty to her father is now transferred to you. She said she thought I ought to have spoken to you both in the first instance. Of course she is right; but somehow it seems rather absurd that I am to come to you and formally ask to be received as a suitor for your ward's hand.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: I am glad that love has not totally extinguished your sense of humor, Tavy.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: That answer won't satisfy her.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: My official answer is, obviously, Bless you, my children: may you be happy!
units.name: TANNER

units.text: I wish you would stop playing the fool about this. If it is not serious to you, it is to me, and to her.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: You know very well that she is as free to choose as you. She does not think so.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: She does not think so.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Oh, doesn't she! just! However, say what you want me to do.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: I want you to tell her sincerely and earnestly what you think about me. I want you to tell her that you can trust her to me--that is, if you feel you can.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: I have no doubt that I can trust her to you. What worries me is the idea of trusting you to her. Have you read Maeterlinck's book about the bee?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: keeping his temper with difficulty.
I am not discussing literature at present.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Be just a little patient with me. I am not discussing literature: the book about the bee is natural history. It's an awful lesson to mankind. You think that you are Ann's suitor; that you are the pursuer and she the pursued; that it is your part to woo, to persuade, to prevail, to overcome. Fool: it is you who are the pursued, the marked down quarry, the destined prey. You need not sit looking longingly at the bait through the wires of the trap: the door is open, and will remain so until it shuts behind you for ever.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: I wish I could believe that, vilely as you put it.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Why, man, what other work has she in life but to get a husband? It is a woman's business to get married as soon as possible, and a man's to keep unmarried as long as he can. You have your poems and your tragedies to work at: Ann has nothing.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: I cannot write without inspiration. And nobody can give me that except Ann.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Well, hadn't you better get it from her at a safe distance? Petrarch didn't see half as much of Laura, nor Dante of Beatrice, as you see of Ann now; and yet they wrote first-rate poetry--at least so I'm told. They never exposed their idolatry to the test of domestic familiarity; and it lasted them to their graves. Marry Ann and at the end of a week you'll find no more inspiration than in a plate of muffins.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: You think I shall tire of her.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Not at all: you don't get tired of muffins. But you don't find inspiration in them; and you won't in her when she ceases to be a poet's dream and becomes a solid eleven stone wife. You'll be forced to dream about somebody else; and then there will be a row.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: This sort of talk is no use, Jack. You don't understand. You have never been in love.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: I! I have never been out of it. Why, I am in love even with Ann. But I am neither the slave of love nor its dupe. Go to the bee, thou poet: consider her ways and be wise. By Heaven, Tavy, if women could do without our work, and we ate their children's bread instead of making it, they would kill us as the spider kills her mate or as the bees kill the drone. And they would be right if we were good for nothing but love.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Ah, if we were only good enough for Love! There is nothing like Love: there is nothing else but Love: without it the world would be a dream of sordid horror.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: And this--this is the man who asks me to give him the hand of my ward! Tavy: I believe we were changed in our cradles, and that you are the real descendant of Don Juan.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: I beg you not to say anything like that to Ann.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Don't be afraid. She has marked you for her own; and nothing will stop her now. You are doomed.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Straker comes back with a newspaper.
